context:
Hashing is cheap and deterministic; use sha256 so short IDs are
stable across pipeline runs. The collision-extension rule is the
only nuance - implement it as a second pass over the first-pass
dict: sort entries, find collisions, extend both sides by 2 chars
until unique, repeat.

The frontend load pattern: fetch short_ids.json on first navigation
to /results/compare, cache in module scope. For the
Matrix → Compare flow, the short_id is already on each PlatformRow
so no extra fetch is needed.
description:
The current Compare URL format is
`/results/compare?ids=<full_result_id>,<full_result_id>,...`.

Full result IDs average ~40 characters (e.g.,
`tpch-duckdb-sf0.01-20260403-7fe93365`). With 4+ selections plus the
base URL, encoded commas, and any future additional query params, the
URL approaches 2KB. Chrome handles this, but proxies, older browsers,
and CDN caches have been observed to truncate or reject URLs above
1024 bytes. Once the matrix leaderboard ships and users can
one-click-compare 6-8 platforms, this becomes a real failure mode.

This TODO introduces a short-ID scheme: a stable 8-character prefix
of a deterministic hash of the full result_id. The pipeline emits a
lookup table `short_ids.json` mapping short → full; the frontend
resolves both directions.

Collision handling: if two short IDs collide in the active corpus,
the pipeline extends the colliding pair to 10 chars (and so on). This
is logged at build time. At current corpus scale (12 bundles) and
foreseeable scale (hundreds), 8 chars is effectively collision-free,
but the extend-on-collision rule is required for robustness.

anti_patterns.dont: pre-emptively encode short IDs in /results/r/<id> paths

anti_patterns.instead: unknown IDs fall through to normal 404 handling
anti_patterns.why: a stale bookmark should still try to resolve gracefully

anti_patterns.dont: use a random or timestamp-based short ID
anti_patterns.why: it would change on each pipeline run and break shared links

preserves.behavior: Direct links to /results/r/<full_result_id> remain unchanged - this TODO only affects Compare query params
Existing long-form Compare URLs continue to work - backward compatible
Pipeline remains a single pass - short-ID generation piggybacks on the existing bundle-id enumeration

work_units.notes:
For each result_id, compute sha256(result_id)[:8]. Build a dict
{short: full}; on collision, extend both entries to 10 chars,
then 12, up to 16. Emit to
results-explorer/public/data/short_ids.json.
